channel.title: Brendon Roberto
channel.description: Game development deep dives, Fiber dev logs, art and experiments.

item.title: Sketchbook
item.description: Hypnos from first sketch to 3D, early Rubbley concept art, characters, paintings, figure studies, pixel art and older traditional work.

item.title: Learning the Fourier transform
item.description: A sine-wave mixer with a live Fourier transform, and how the FFT splits and recombines to get fast.

item.title: Living fringe
item.description: Grass, moss and ivy that sway in the wind and bend away from whoever walks through them: Stephen Cassidy’s design, and how it shipped.

item.title: Fiber
item.description: A four-player co-op platformer where the whole world is sewn from thread: the world, the Fiberkin and the systems underneath.

item.title: How Rubbley’s gravity works
item.description: The Newtonian physics behind Rubbley, the small game tweaks layered on top, and the GDScript that implements them, with diagrams and an orbit simulator you can play with.

item.title: Sewing Fiber’s UI
item.description: How Fiber’s menus, HUD, shop and auction house became fabric patches: the prototypes, the rules they settled, and screenshots from along the way.

item.title: Sketch to sprite
item.description: A local image-generation pipeline for pixel-art drafts: the fight to keep characters on model, a lot of failed animation attempts, and the hand cleanup in Aseprite. Every image is labeled as generated.

item.title: Fiber’s software factory
item.description: How a loose idea becomes a merged feature: wayfinder maps, plans merged before issues, a scheduled agent and scripted playtests.

item.title: Making hits land
item.description: Fiber’s data-driven enemies, and the small effects that make combat feel good: damage numbers, hit flash, screenshake, i-frames and hitstop.

item.title: Remembering things
item.description: Maps that remember what you did when you warp away, and a save system that writes locally first and syncs to Nakama.

item.title: Two players, one map
item.description: Fiber’s first working multiplayer session: a Nakama backend, a host-authoritative game, and the bugs that showed up first.

item.title: Drafting dungeons
item.description: Fiber’s endgame: crafted dungeon keys, a party that drafts rooms card by card, and Stephen Cassidy’s door UI.

item.title: Skills you sew
item.description: Emblems: skills as craftable items you weave, embroider and use as keys, and the first skill effect, Ember Slash.

item.title: Stats and affixes
item.description: Fiber’s RPG stat system, graded item affixes, thread-based crafting and the equipment screen that shows it all.

item.title: Fiber’s first month
item.description: Starting a co-op platformer from Godot’s starter tutorial and Kenney placeholder art: a player state machine, one-way platforms, tests in CI and maps that connect.
